response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB / HCT) AS r FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT > 0 GROUP BY ID), a AS (SELECT ID, r, r - (SELECT AVG(r) FROM p) AS d1 FROM p WHERE r > (SELECT AVG(r) FROM p)), b AS (SELECT ID, r, d1, r - (SELECT AVG(r) FROM a) AS d2 FROM a WHERE r > (SELECT AVG(r) FROM a)) SELECT AVG(r) AS avg_ratio, AVG(d1) AS avg_above_overall, AVG(d2) AS avg_above_group FROM b;

assumptions.assumption: A patient has many lab rows, so each patient's ratio is the mean of HGB/HCT over all their lab tests with both values present and HCT > 0. The overall average is then the mean of these per-patient ratios, so each patient counts equally.
'Above the group's own average' means above the average ratio of the patients who passed the first filter. Strictly greater than is used for both filters.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each lab test record as a unit: compute HGB/HCT per record, with no per-patient aggregation. The averages are then taken over individual records, so patients with more tests weigh more.
